clues.title: Pole: Pole
text: Square poles with small holes running from bottom to top are distinctive to Thailand. In Sri Lanka, similar poles exist, but the holes are limited to the top part of the pole.
Note: You can find same poles in Laos(but Laos drives right and most cities coverage is done with google car with roofrack)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Concrete road
text: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Sign: Sign Posts
text: Signposts in Thailand are **square** and **bulky** in shape, usually **white**, and often have the **bottom painted black**.
**NOTE:** In Southeast Asia, this design is unique to Thailand.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Thailand has yellow middle lines. These middle lines are either solid or dashed lines.
**NOTE:** Malaysia only has white middle lines.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: หยุด
text: Stop signs in Thailand always have the word "Stop" written in Thai (หยุด).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Nakhon Vibes
text: Brown paved roads among fields of sugarcane, cassava, and corn can be found in southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Krabi Rocks
text: Western Krabi and parts of eastern Phang-nga also feature large exposed rock mountains running north-south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Khao Sok National Park
text: Khao Sok National Park in northern Phang-nga and western Surat Thani features some of the tallest and steepest exposed rock mountains in the south of Thailand. The mountains generally run east-west.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park
text: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park in western Prachuap Khiri Khan features large, distinct exposed rock mountain massifs. Notably, the mountains can be seen from the center of the province.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mukdahan
text: The province of Mukdahan features many long, low hills among fields of rice, sugarcane, cassava and rubber trees.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Chaiyaphum

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: North Saraburi Mountains

clues.title: Landscape: Lopburi Mountains

clues.title: Landscape: Phetchabun Valley

clues.title: Landscape: Tak Hills

clues.title: Landscape: Doi Luang Chiang Dao

clues.title: Landscape: Phrao Valley
text: The Phrao District in Chiang Mai is a fairly flat valley surrounded by mountains in all directions. The valley will commonly grow rice and fruit.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Rocky Mountains

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Smooth Mountains

clues.title: Landscape: Tall Mountains
text: Tall mountains are most often seen in northwestern Thailand.
NOTE: Some parts of the southern peninsular part are also mountainous.

clues.title: Dry Flatland
text: Thailand has two regions that are relatively flat and dry compared to other areas. One north of Bangkok, the other more east.
NOTE: The eastern area feels sometimes a bit drier than the area north of Bangkok.

clues.title: Thailand
text: Thai landline phone numbers have 9 digits. The first digits of phone numbers are the area code. The Bangkok area code is 02, the other area codes have three digits. The area codes are grouped, so even just learning the first digit is useful.
NOTE: Mobile phone numbers start with 08 or 09 and have 10 digits. None of these numbers overlap with the area codes. Numbers starting with 06 are also not regional.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Insulators 7 or more ridges
text: Insulators with 7 or more ridges are found in the southern half of the peninsula, as well as highways in Chiang Rai and Phayao.
